subject.title: fix(context-engine): bound deferred turn maintenance with a per-task timeout (AI-assisted)

question: Should OpenClaw core expose and own `agents.defaults.compaction.turnMaintenanceTaskTimeoutMs` plus the abandoned-worker fence/checkpoint lifecycle for third-party context engines?
rationale: The patch is intentionally opt-in, but it adds a public persistent policy knob and defines core behavior after a plugin-owned maintenance operation has timed out; source evidence cannot determine the desired long-term product and ownership contract.

options.title: Adopt the opt-in core contract
options.body: Merge the bounded deferred-maintenance policy with the disabled-by-default configuration and fence/checkpoint protections after normal current-head validation.

options.title: Keep recovery policy centralized
options.body: Decline this new configuration surface and instead define a narrower generic session-recovery or context-engine lifecycle contract before implementing a timeout.

options.title: Move timeout ownership to engines
options.body: Require context-engine plugins to expose their own bounded-maintenance behavior and keep core responsible only for generic session coordination.

recommendation.title: Adopt the opt-in core contract
recommendation.body: Merge the bounded deferred-maintenance policy with the disabled-by-default configuration and fence/checkpoint protections after normal current-head validation.

likelyOwner.reason: They authored the proposed contract and can clarify the intended lifecycle, though a core-area owner must make the final product decision.
